claim: On the identical EdgeCases input, disrobe recovers at least as many recompile-clean main-class methods under real javac as JADX and CFR, with no original-jar classpath leak.
detail: `disrobe` leads the JAR leg at 131/131 clean methods vs CFR's 105/106. On the DEX leg, JADX has the higher clean-rate (98.5% vs 97.7%) while `disrobe` emits one more clean method (129 vs 128). All rows use the same stubbed real-`javac` oracle and are recompile-only.

oracle.external: real javac (JDK), per-method recompile error-free against a STUBBED (empty) classpath so a wrong recovered signature cannot resolve against the original classes; the SAME oracle scores every tool
oracle.note: recompile-only: each method body compiles clean, not asserted byte-equivalent. The STRONG asserted JVM number is the 131/131 per-method recompile gate (jvm-javac descriptor). Both decompilers emit synthetic accessor/lambda/bridge methods, so the per-tool emitted-method count differs by design; the comparable number is the recompile-clean rate plus the absolute clean-method count.

reproduce: cargo run -p disrobe-bench-head-to-head  (needs javac + jadx + cfr on PATH; cfr.jar via evidence/competitors/install-linux.sh)
title: APK / DEX decompilation: disrobe vs JADX vs CFR
